title: Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: A conflict between China and Japan that began in earnest with a clash at the Marco Polo Bridge on July 7, 1937, after Japan's expanding influence in China since 1931. It involved rapid Japanese conquests, including the Nanjing Massacre, then stalemate, and ended with Japan's defeat in 1945. China suffered some 15 million deaths.

as_recorded.value: between 1937 and 1945, China and Japan were at total war

reviewer_note: Sources suggest the conflict may be dated from 1931, while the main war is dated 1937–1945. The end date of 1945 is given only as a year; the Wikidata lead of 9 September 1945 is not confirmed by the sources. Casualty figures are as stated (up to 300,000 at Nanjing; some 15 million overall).. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Encyclopaedia Britannica, history.ox.ac.uk; quotes machine-checked.)
